page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine featuring a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation and 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor configured with 8 shared vCPUs across 4 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. System memory consists of 40.0 GB of RAM, providing 5.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in specific machine learning workloads, with LLM inference speeds reaching 9944.32 tokens per second for prompt processing and 464.42 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing registers at 3147.67 tokens per second and text generation at 107.73 tokens per second. Standard compute benchmarks fall into the average tier, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1786.68 and a multi-core score of 14175.12. Memory bandwidth tests show 784.94 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 88.57 GB/sec for large-block reads.

The fractional GPU allocation offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated card. However, the shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GHz clock speed present a tradeoff, resulting in average general-purpose compute performance. This server type is suited for small to medium LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, database operations, and applications requiring moderate GPU acceleration alongside NVMe storage.
